constraints.evidence: Slide 15 tests the company-level floor, not just product margin: 'Requests per account a month at a 75% margin 5,296 = (25% × $60.49M − $12.67M − $0.6M) ÷ (3,234 × $0.009 × 12)', and 74.1% at paywall-buyer usage. The 5,300 cap is in the headline.

Slide 14: '$2.89M is 5.0 percentage points of today's $57.6M ARR; the 4 percentage point gap needs $2.30M'. It also says 'Pro lifts NRR once' and that lower mobile churn is what holds 105%. Slide 10 counts mobile churn against the plan.

Slides 12 and 15 give inference cost at $17.10, $32.40, $61.20 and $130.50 a month. They give add-on margins of 58.9% and 12.4% and say the top 10% send 58% of requests. Pro contribution is net of inference ($1.3M).
The $0.6M platform, evaluation and support cost is deducted in both contribution figures: Pro $1.03M and add-on $0.84M. It is treated as cost of revenue in the margin test.
Slide 14: 'Build: $1.47M (14 engineers for two quarters at $210K a year), repaid in about 17 months'. The $1.0M headline is labelled 'before the one-off build'.

Mobile versus Copilot is the core of the recommendation. Slide 8 gives 27% versus 6% churn and 38% versus 19% feature ranking. Slide 10 gives $544K versus $281K per quarter and a 52% break-even. Staffing is shown on slide 17, with the 14-engineer assumption flagged.
Slides 4–5: 14% against 46%, $2.45M against $8.06M, 1,372 buyers. 'Even the paywall rate is a ceiling'. Sample seat sizes of 9.4, 8.1 and 6.2 are shown, with the 6% response rate.

Slide 15 footnote 2: 'Inference at $0.009 per request is fixed through December 2027; the 35% fall in list prices over 12 months is upside from 2028 only'. All margin maths uses $0.009, and renegotiation is a next step.
Slide 9: 1,560 × 7 pp × $5,877.6 = $0.6M a year 'an upper bound'. It notes Routewise's 20% discount in the same quarter and that loss-note mentions are not cause.

alternatives.evidence: This is the recommended option (Pro at +$12 per seat with an allowance). Slides 13–15 give 3,234 accounts and $2.89M ARR, $1.03M contribution, margin by usage level and the 5,296 request allowance. The document does not give the ~56% tier margin at mean usage.

Only the flat $149 add-on is evaluated: $2.45M ARR, $0.84M contribution, 58.9% and 12.4% margins. The rejection reason 'Nobody: heavy and light users pay the same flat fee' ignores the usage-charge or lower-entry-price variant. That variant is never costed. Pro beats the add-on only at 33% adoption: at 14%, Pro adds just $0.09M after costs.

This is the recommendation: mobile first, Copilot in Q4 2027. Slides 8–10 quantify the cost of waiting ($281K per quarter), the 4.5x churn ratio and the 52% flip point. It keeps paying beta accounts served and runs a Pro price test on random non-beta accounts, which gives the non-volunteer demand read.
There is no mention of bundling Copilot into Core at no charge, either as a capped defensive bundle or otherwise.

sensitivities.evidence: Slide 14 gives Pro at 14% ($1.22M ARR, $0.09M after costs), 33% ($2.89M) and 46% ($4.02M). It states the flip point: 'Pro … covers the NRR target, if at least 26% of accounts move' (gate 26.3%). It compares add-on at 14% ($2.45M) against the survey's $8.06M. The add-on's own thresholds (13% for NRR, 6% for run cost, 20% for year-one payback) are not shown.

Slide 15 gives margin by usage (74.1% at 6,800 requests) and the break point of 5,296 requests per Pro account, which is also gate 2. Slide 12 gives add-on margin by usage level. The price after December 2027 is not varied. Pro contribution at 6,800 requests is not stated; it works out to about −$0.1M.

The win-rate benefit is bounded at $0.6M a year, with the sales memo refuted ('3.0 times what the whole drop is worth'). Mobile versus AI is shown per quarter ($544K versus $281K). The flip point is explicit: 'mobile first holds while the rewrite removes at least 52% of mobile churn'. The $0.6M is an upper bound, not a range by share attributed to AI. A variant on the 1,190 churned accounts that gave a reason is also shown (1.8x).

overclaim.quote: Copilot should wait for the mobile rewrite, whose delay puts nearly twice as much ARR at risk (slide 10: 'nearly twice as much ARR at risk as a quarter's wait for Copilot')

omissions: The '1.9x' comparison leaves out the document's own $257K per quarter of deferred Pro contribution. Adding it to the $281.4K Copilot side gives about $538K against $544K for mobile, which is roughly break-even, not nearly twice. Slide 10 mentions the $257K but the headline ignores it.

Pro contribution at the usage that paying adopters actually show (6,800 requests a month) is not stated. At 3,234 accounts it is about −$0.09M a year (ARR $2.89M, inference $2.38M, run cost $0.6M). The $1.0M headline uses the 3,600-request beta mean instead. The document gives only the 74.1% margin figure.

At the document's own 14% adoption, Pro makes $0.09M a year after costs, so the $1.47M build would not be repaid. The 17-month payback holds only at 33% adoption. The document does not say what happens if the Pro price test shows adoption near 14%.
The decision line 'hold the Q2 launch unless the January check fails gate 3' contradicts the governing thought of a Q4 2027 launch. It is unclear which launch date is being approved.
The document does not say how Q4 2027 Pro migration can lift NRR to 105% 'by 2028' when the migration takes 12 months after launch. The NRR path and timing are not shown.
unsupported_assumptions: 'If 33% move up as in 2023, Pro adds $2.9M of ARR': the 2023 tier precedent is applied to a different tier at a new price, and the paywall evidence (14%) is the only revealed demand for Copilot.
'3,600 requests a month per account (beta mean)' for all Pro accounts: paying adopters averaged 6,800 requests, so this assumption carries the $1.0M contribution headline.
'the rewrite ends mobile-reliability churn when it ships': this is the basis for the 1.9x figure, and the pack gives no evidence of how much churn the rewrite removes.

'Assumes the rewrite needs these 14 engineers for the same two quarters Copilot would have taken': the plan's staffing and the Q4 2027 launch date rest on this. It is flagged as something to confirm and has no stated basis in the pack.
Copilot side of the timing comparison: 'Copilot wins back the whole Q3 drop and every AI-driven switch'. This is an upper bound the document itself says is inflated by Routewise's 20% discount.
